cards.name: Grain
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that lays procedural, film-style grain over everything below it without touching the pixels: Amount sets how visible the grain is, Size how big each grain is, Roughness how irregular and clumpy it looks, and the seed picks another random pattern. Its controls and defaults (Size 25, Roughness 50) match the Grain panel of Camera Raw; at the default Amount 0 it does nothing. The harvest has no slider ranges (the descriptor stores any 16-bit integer); 0-100 is the expected dialog range from Camera Raw, not verified.
use_for: filmic texture on a clean digital or AI-generated image so it reads as shot on film
matching grain across composited elements so a pasted cut-out sits in the background plate
breaking up banding in smooth skies and gradients before print or video export
retro poster or editorial photo finish
avoid: script values outside the dialog range: the descriptor accepts any 16-bit integer (1e6 read back as 16960) and does not clamp; keep Amount, Size and Roughness inside 0-100
fine grain on an image shown small (feed thumbnail, mobile): Size near the default 25 disappears when downscaled; raise Size, or use Filter > Noise > Add Noise for coarse digital noise
grain that must change every frame in a video or GIF: set a different grainSeed per frame

params.name: Amount
params.does: strength / visibility of the grain; 0 (default) means no grain
params.typical: 15-40 subtle, 60-90 heavy

params.name: Size
params.does: size of the individual grain particles
params.typical: 25 default; 40-70 for coarse grain that survives downscaling

params.name: Roughness
params.does: how uneven the grain is: low = fine and regular, high = irregular and clumpy
params.typical: 50 default; 60-80 for a gritty film stock

params.name: grainSeed
params.does: random seed of the grain pattern; another value gives another pattern
params.typical: 0 default; any integer

pairs_with: a Levels or Curves adjustment layer with lifted blacks for a faded film tone
Hue/Saturation (Colorize or desaturated) for a black-and-white film look
Photo Filter for a warm vintage cast
cards.scripting: var s=stringIDToTypeID, d=new ActionDescriptor(), r=new ActionReference(); r.putClass(s('adjustmentLayer')); d.putReference(s('null'), r); var a=new ActionDescriptor(); a.putInteger(s('grainAmount'), 80); a.putInteger(s('grainSize'), 60); a.putInteger(s('grainRoughness'), 70); a.putInteger(s('grainSeed'), 0); var l=new ActionDescriptor(); l.putObject(s('type'), s('grainAdjustment'), a); d.putObject(s('using'), s('adjustmentLayer'), l); executeAction(s('make'), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: yes: an adjustment layer, editable, maskable and removable without touching the pixels below
cards.cost: low: procedural grain recalculated live for the layers below; no pixel data stored

review.changes: summary: the Camera Raw comparison now rests on the harvested defaults (Size 25, Roughness 50) instead of an untested behaviour claim; the 0-100 range stays flagged as unverified

verified.note: Strong monochrome grain over the whole frame, clearly visible on the 1:1 crop (mean change 13.6 levels, the noise is the same in all three channels) and still visible at 960x540.

cards.name: Hue/Saturation
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that shifts the hue, saturation and lightness of everything below, either for the whole image (Master) or for one colour range (Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues, Magentas); with Colorize on it discards the original hues and tints the whole image in one hue, a single-colour monochrome. The master and per-range amounts travel in the Adjustment list (hueSatAdjustmentV2 objects) whose inner keys the harvest did not read.
use_for: recolouring one colour range, e.g. turning a red dress or product blue through the Reds range
global desaturation or a saturation boost for a mood grade
single-hue tinted background photo for a poster or social post via Colorize
toning down one clashing colour in a layout photo
avoid: exact brand-colour matching: hue shifts are relative and catch skin tones too; use a Solid Color fill layer in Color blend mode with a mask
black-and-white conversion with control over how each colour maps to grey: use the Black & White adjustment
large hue shifts on low-saturation or JPEG-compressed areas band and blotch; mask to the object
Colorize at its default hue: a rose-pink monotone, not a sepia; set the hue (hue 38 with saturation 28 gave a brown sepia) (plan runs 2026-10-15 (photo_looks.sepia_vintage))

params.name: Colorize
params.does: on = replace every hue with one tint (single-colour monochrome); off = shift the existing hues
params.typical: false for corrections, true for a tinted monochrome look

params.name: Adjustment
params.does: list of hueSatAdjustmentV2 objects holding the master and per-range hue / saturation / lightness amounts (inner keys not harvested; plan runs 2026-10-15 (photo_looks.sepia_vintage) set them as the integers hue, saturation and lightness inside one hueSatAdjustmentV2 object: 38, 28, 0 for a sepia brown)
params.typical: hueSatAdjustmentV2 (the current format)

params.name: Preset Kind
params.does: where the settings come from: the default, a factory or user preset (loaded through Using) or custom values
params.typical: presetKindCustom when a script sets the values

params.name: Using
params.does: path of a saved Hue/Saturation preset file to load
params.typical: only with a factory or user preset

cards.demo_note: Colorize alone: the plate should turn single-hue monochrome (a tint, or plain grey if the stored colorize saturation is 0); the exact tint of a scripted Colorize without amounts was not tested.
pairs_with: a layer mask or clipping to one layer to recolour a single object
Grain for a tinted vintage photo
Selective Color for fine ink-level tweaks after the big hue move

verified.note: Colorize at its default hue gives a red-brown monotone (every colour block becomes a muted red), the single-hue tint the card describes.

cards.name: Invert
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that flips every channel value below it to its opposite, giving a photographic negative: lights go dark, darks go light and each colour turns into its complement (red to cyan, blue to yellow). It has no settings.
use_for: photo-negative or X-ray style poster art
turning black-on-white line art or a scanned sketch into white-on-black
a colour-negative accent through a mask for a glitch or psychedelic layout
spotting differences between two aligned versions together with the Difference blend mode
avoid: scanned colour film negatives: a plain invert leaves the orange film mask; convert in Camera Raw or with per-channel Curves
inverting brightness but keeping the hues: set the Invert layer to the Luminosity blend mode
CMYK documents invert each ink, which looks different from the RGB result
pairs_with: Threshold or Black & White for a high-contrast negative graphic
Luminosity blend mode to invert tones only
a layer mask to invert part of the image

cards.non_destructive: yes: an adjustment layer, editable, maskable and removable without touching the pixels below
cards.cost: low: recalculated live for the layers below; adds no pixel data to the file

verified.note: Full negative: the grey ramp reverses (5..249 to 249..5) and every block turns to its complement (red to cyan, blue to yellow).

cards.name: Levels
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that remaps tones by setting input black point, white point and midtone gamma (and output black / white) for the composite or each channel against a histogram: pulling the black and white points in adds contrast, moving gamma brightens or darkens the midtones, per-channel moves remove colour casts. Auto applies Photoshop's automatic correction. The point values travel in the Adjustment list: one levelsAdjustment per channel with channel, input [black, white], gamma and output [black, white].
use_for: fixing a flat, washed-out photo or video frame by setting black and white points
neutralising a colour cast with per-channel levels or the grey-point eyedropper
cleaning a scan of line art or handwriting to solid black on white
faded, matte blacks for a film look via output levels
avoid: shaping one tonal range (S-curve, protecting highlights): use Curves
big point moves on 8-bit images leave histogram gaps and banding; work in 16-bit or move modestly
Auto on deliberately dark or bright moody images normalises the range and flattens the mood; set the points by hand

scripts: "auto": true in the make adjustmentLayer descriptor is ignored (the gallery read no auto key back and the layer changed nothing); for an automatic correction run the destructive levels event with autoBlackWhite / autoNeutrals, or set the points in the Adjustment object

params.name: Auto
params.does: true = apply Photoshop's automatic levels correction (the Auto button)
params.typical: true for a quick fix

params.name: Adjustment
params.does: levelsAdjustment list, one per channel: channel (reference), input [black, white], gamma, output [black, white]
params.typical: input black about 20 and white about 235 with gamma 1.1 for a flat photo

params.name: Preset Kind
params.does: where the settings come from: the default, a factory or user preset (loaded through Using) or custom values
params.typical: presetKindCustom when a script sets the values

params.name: Using
params.does: path of a saved Levels preset file to load
params.typical: only with a factory or user preset

pairs_with: Curves for finer tonal shaping after Levels sets the range
Hue/Saturation after the tones are fixed
Grain with raised output black for a faded film finish
cards.scripting: var s=stringIDToTypeID, d=new ActionDescriptor(), r=new ActionReference(); r.putClass(s('adjustmentLayer')); d.putReference(s('null'), r); var a=new ActionDescriptor(); a.putEnumerated(s('presetKind'), s('presetKindType'), s('presetKindCustom')); var lv=new ActionDescriptor(), ch=new ActionReference(); ch.putEnumerated(s('channel'), s('channel'), s('composite')); lv.putReference(s('channel'), ch); var inp=new ActionList(); inp.putInteger(30); inp.putInteger(220); lv.putList(s('input'), inp); lv.putDouble(s('gamma'), 1.2); var adj=new ActionList(); adj.putObject(s('levelsAdjustment'), lv); a.putList(s('adjustment'), adj); var l=new ActionDescriptor(); l.putObject(s('type'), s('levels'), a); d.putObject(s('using'), s('adjustmentLayer'), l); executeAction(s('make'), d, DialogModes.NO); /* the structure the gallery rendered (input 30 / 220, gamma 1.2); 'auto' is ignored by make, see avoid */
cards.non_destructive: yes: an adjustment layer, editable, maskable and removable without touching the pixels below
cards.cost: low: recalculated live for the layers below; adds no pixel data to the file

review.changes: demo_settings: added Preset Kind presetKindCustom so the spec matches the scripting call; removed the demo note duplicated in avoid (demo_note keeps it). Demo stays weak: Auto is the only settable switch

verified.note: Levels 30 / 1.2 / 220 applied exactly (frame within 0.6 levels of the formula): plate tones at or below 30 clip to black, at or above 220 to white (pure black pixels 1.6 % -> 9.2 %, pure white 1.5 % -> 4.0 %), mid grey brightens 127 -> 146: more contrast and brighter midtones, no colour shift.

previous.note: Untested: frame identical to the plate (diff 0.0): Photoshop dropped "Auto" from the make descriptor (index "dropped") and read Preset Kind back as default, so no levels change happened; the black / white / gamma points live in the unharvested Adjustment object.

second_opinion.note: Frame vs ref diff 0.0 confirmed in index.json: nothing was applied, so the effect is untested rather than broken; the card text is not contradicted by the frame.

cards.name: OpenColorIO Transform
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that applies an OpenColorIO (OCIO) colour transform, such as a colour-space conversion or a view / look transform from the active OCIO config, to the layers below. The menu item is hidden unless a document using OCIO colour management is open, and the harvest found no adjustment class for it, so its settings and script route are unknown; this description comes from general knowledge of OCIO workflows and was not tested.
use_for: VFX and film pipelines: converting plates between colour spaces (e.g. ACES) inside an OCIO-managed document
previewing or baking a show look / LUT defined in the studio's OCIO config
avoid: ordinary sRGB or print design work: the item does not appear without an OCIO document; use Color Lookup or Curves for creative grading
scripted pipelines: no harvested event or settings (see scripting)
pairs_with: an OCIO-managed document (prerequisite)
cards.scripting: No harvested script route: the harvest found no adjustment class for this item; the candidate event 'adjustmentLayerOCIOAdjustment' is unverified. The menu command id is 6650 (visible only with an OCIO document open); running it from a script is untested and would open the dialog.
cards.non_destructive: the harvest lists it as a non-destructive adjustment layer; not probed further

verified.note: Untested: status hidden (the item appears only with an OCIO-managed document and has no harvested class), so it was not rendered.

second_opinion.note: No frame on disk and the id is listed in not_rendered.json / failed.json; the reason given matches the card status and the harvest.

cards.name: Photo Filter
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that imitates a coloured filter on a camera lens: it blends the filter colour into everything below at the chosen Density, warming (orange), cooling (blue) or tinting the image; with Preserve Luminosity on, the image keeps its brightness so only the colour cast changes.
use_for: warm golden-hour or cool moonlit mood on a photo
unifying the colour temperature of composited elements
correcting a cast with the complementary filter, e.g. a blue filter on a tungsten-orange shot
brand-colour wash across a photo for a social post
avoid: exact neutral colour correction: use Curves / Levels with the grey eyedropper or Camera Raw white balance
a strong graphic two-colour look: use Gradient Map
script Density past 100%: the descriptor stores any value (1e6 kept as sent) and the harvest records no min / max; stay at or below 100

params.name: Filter Color
params.does: the filter colour (stored as Lab); the default is an orange warming colour (Lab 67.06 / 32 / 120)
params.typical: orange to warm, a saturated blue such as #006DFF to cool

params.name: Density
params.does: strength of the tint in percent
params.typical: 25 default; 40-70 for an obvious grade

params.name: Preserve Luminosity
params.does: true keeps the brightness so the filter does not darken the image
params.typical: true

pairs_with: Grain and a Levels fade for a vintage photo
a layer mask to tint only the sky or background
Hue/Saturation to pull back saturation after a strong filter

verified.note: Blue #006DFF at density 60 pulls the warm photo to a cool lavender cast while the grey ramp keeps its brightness (Preserve Luminosity), as described.

cards.name: Posterize
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that cuts each colour channel down to the set number of brightness Levels, so smooth gradations snap into flat bands of colour; low values give a bold screen-print / pop-art look with hard colour edges (4 levels per RGB channel leave at most 64 colours).
use_for: screen-print or pop-art poster from a photo
flat-colour base for vector tracing or a limited-palette illustration
retro comic or stencil look together with Threshold or a halftone
seeing the tonal zones of a photo, paint-by-numbers style
avoid: soft or noisy photos give ragged, speckled band edges: run Filter > Noise > Median or a blur first
a palette of colours you choose: Posterize picks levels per channel, not your colours; use Gradient Map or Indexed Color
high values (above about 20) barely change an 8-bit photo; use 2-8 for a visible look

params.name: Levels
params.does: number of brightness levels per channel; fewer levels = fewer, flatter bands
params.typical: 4 default; 2-6 for graphic looks, 8-12 for subtle

pairs_with: a Median or blur pass first for clean band edges
Gradient Map above it to swap the bands for brand colours
Threshold on a copy for a black key line

verified.note: Four levels per channel: hard flat colour bands, the grey ramp in four steps and the blocks snapped to 0/85/170/255 values: the screen-print look.

cards.name: Selective Color
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that changes the amount of cyan, magenta, yellow and black in one colour family at a time (Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues, Magentas, Whites, Neutrals, Blacks) and leaves the rest alone; Relative scales the ink already there, Absolute adds or removes a fixed percentage, so Absolute is stronger. The per-range amounts travel in the Color Correction list, one colorCorrection per family: colors (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks), cyan, magenta, yellowColor, black.
use_for: refining skin tones through Reds / Yellows without touching the background
making a brand colour richer or nudging it toward a print swatch
removing a cast from whites or neutrals, or deepening blacks through the Blacks range
film-style split grade: cool Neutrals / Blacks, warm Whites
avoid: big hue swaps: Hue/Saturation moves hue further and faster
Relative on a colour holding almost none of that ink does nothing; use Absolute

Reds is a wide family: Reds cyan +50 also pulled red out of the orange (255 -> 196), yellow (255 -> 233) and pink-magenta (224 -> 167) bars in the gallery frame; mask it, or balance with Yellows / Magentas
read-backs name the Reds family 'radius' (a shared type id); send 'reds'

params.name: Method
params.does: relative = changes ink in proportion to what is there; absolute = adds or subtracts a fixed percentage (stronger)
params.typical: relative for subtle work, absolute for a visible shift

params.name: Color Correction
params.does: list of per-range ink amounts, one colorCorrection per family: colors (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks), cyan, magenta, yellowColor, black
params.typical: e.g. Reds: less cyan, more yellow for warmer skin

params.name: Preset Kind
params.does: where the settings come from: the default, a factory or user preset (loaded through Using) or custom values
params.typical: presetKindCustom when a script sets the values

params.name: Using
params.does: path of a saved Selective Color preset file to load
params.typical: only with a factory or user preset

pairs_with: Hue/Saturation for the big moves, Selective Color for the fine ink balance
a layer mask on skin or product
Levels / Curves to fix tone first

cards.name: Threshold
cards.summary: Adjustment layer that turns everything below into pure black and white: pixels brighter than the Level become white, darker ones black, with no greys or colour left; a hard stencil / photocopy look.
use_for: stencil, street-art or rubber-stamp graphic from a photo
preparing a photo or scan for vector tracing, one-colour print or laser engraving
finding the darkest and lightest points of an image (slide Level to the ends) before Levels / Curves
clean black-on-white line art from a pencil scan
avoid: soft or noisy photos break into blotchy edges; raise contrast, sharpen or blur first
you need greys as dots: use Filter > Pixelate > Color Halftone or Bitmap mode with a halftone screen
two colours other than black and white: add a Gradient Map above it

params.name: Level
params.does: brightness cut-off: lighter pixels turn white, darker turn black
params.typical: 128 default; 100-160 depending on the image's midtones

pairs_with: a Gaussian Blur or Median pass first for smoother shapes
Gradient Map above it for a two-colour print
Image Trace in Illustrator afterwards
